1.title: Katarina Mogus dives deep on Adobe + YouTube workflows
1.author: Creator Insider
1.hook: Adobe + YouTube partnership on Premiere mobile: dedicated Shorts templates, mobile editing features, and barrier-to-entry changes for creators. Features a creator (@katamogz) walking through her workflow and Adobe's product lead discussing what's coming next.

1.title: AI Will Automate 50% of Digital Work in Years | Brendan Foody
1.author: MTS
1.hook: Brendan Foody (Mercor co-founder) on why post-training evals are the bottleneck for frontier models, why RL saturates benchmarks quickly, and why AI hasn't yet become reliable virtual coworkers despite the hype.

1.title: Black October Proved AI Cyber Threats Are Real | Varin Nair
1.author: MTS
1.hook: Varin Nair (Factory) discusses how open-weight models and agent frameworks have automated cyberattacks at nation-state scale, Factory's pivot into offensive security via War Games, and why defensive engineering needs deterministic automated triage loops.

1.title: Humanoid Robots Could Arrive by 2027 | Max Poff
1.author: MTS
1.hook: Stack AI founders discuss moving enterprise AI agents from demos to production—air-gapped deployments, engineering stack decisions, Asana integration for scale, and a 2027 timeline for embodied AI.

1.title: Claude Fable 5.2 vs Opus 5.5: When to Use Each Model (Full Tutorial)
1.author: Peter Yang
1.hook: Five concrete use cases comparing Fable 5.2 vs Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (chief of staff, career advisor, workflow automation, mobile app design, end-to-end healthcare support); includes specific prompts and 500+ hours of hands-on comparison.

2.title: Why Enterprise AI Hallucinations Are 5x Higher | Dan Klein
2.author: MTS
2.hook: Dan Klein (UC Berkeley, Scaled Cognition CTO) on why enterprise LLM hallucination rates are 5x higher than reported, why standard token architectures can't enforce safety policies, and how modeling semantic objects changes reliability for agentic AI.

3.title: Claude Code + Obsidian: My family’s AI brain
3.author: How I AI
3.hook: Scott Farrar built a household knowledge base in Claude Code (Markdown files + Obsidian) that pulls insurance docs, appliances, warranties, and family to-do lists; demo shows car insurance shopping workflow, shared system with wife, wall display with recent wins, and approach to AI + math learning where kids teach the AI.

1.title: Why Recursive Self-Improvement Hits a Wall | Ramez Naam
1.author: MTS
1.hook: Ramez Naam argues recursive self-improvement in AI hits empirical diminishing returns, not exponential loops; compares theoretical benchmarks to real task horizons at OpenAI/Anthropic and explains constraints on autonomous AI researchers (data, taste, verification).
